minutes.headline: Board combined the Keating quarry permits and reworked the special event policy; fuel tank request fight
minutes.summary: The Select Board heard tributes to the late Lance May, and the chair announced he will not seek a third term. The board combined the Keating quarry permits into one, approved a BYOB permit, and reworked the draft special event permit policy. Members clashed over the fuel tank item on the state budget-priorities list, and the regional animal control building was discussed without a decision.

public_comment.topic: Introduced a Senate adjournment and governor's citation honoring the late Lance May.
Asked whether open studios need a special event permit, about insurance, and why four events.
Asked for an attendance threshold exemption and a waiver option in the special event policy.
Wants all events to go through the special event process; questioned sleeping trailer permits.
Fuel tanks might be safer elsewhere; urged filing the demolition permit for old primary school.

what_happened.line: The board voted down a motion to remove the DPW fuel tank installation request from the state budget-priorities list, so the request stays on it.
A motion to approve the Keating quarry permit with five conditions, combining three permits under one new number, was made; the minutes do not record the outcome audibly.
The board approved a BYOB license for Waylon Kitchen on Electric Avenue.
The draft special event permit policy was sent back for revision, with town counsel to be asked about liability.
The regional animal control building was discussed without a decision, and the chair announced he will not seek a third term.

why_it_matters: The fuel tank request stays on the list of projects the town asks the state to help fund, so it may affect future capital spending and the town budget, mostly taxes.
The special event policy will decide what permits, insurance and fees apply to local events, and the animal control building is an unresolved cost for the town budget, mostly taxes.
watch_next: The revised special event policy and town counsel's answer on liability are expected to return to the board.
Town Meeting articles were postponed to next week, and the chair's seat and a vacant Planning Board seat go to the May ballot.
